artifacts.summary: Characterizes the lean-extension summary/report skeleton gaps (plain agents have no write stage at all; hard agents have a stage but no inline skeleton) and a new, independently-found defect in all four formal-extension research agents (skeleton present but missing 5 of 8 REPORT_METADATA fields and the Decisions section), with per-file recommendations modelled on general-implementation-agent.md and general-research-agent.md.

memory_candidates.content: When sweeping agent files for artifact-skeleton conformance, don't stop at 'does a report-format/summary-format reference exist' -- an agent can reference the format doc in Context References AND have a named write stage, yet the stage's inline skeleton can still be missing required metadata fields or sections (seen in all four extensions/formal/agents/*-research-agent.md files: skeleton present, but missing Effort/Dependencies/Sources-Inputs/Artifacts/Standards and the Decisions section). Check the fenced skeleton block itself against validate-artifact.sh's REPORT_METADATA/REPORT_SECTIONS arrays field-by-field, not just presence of a skeleton.

validate-artifact.sh's section check is `grep -qE "^##+ ${section}"` (prefix match, any heading depth) and its metadata check is `grep -qF "**${field}**:"` (literal substring anywhere in the file). This means a required section can be satisfied by a nested ### heading elsewhere in the document (e.g. '### Recommendations' under '## Findings' satisfies the 'Recommendations' requirement), and a metadata field can be satisfied by text that appears outside the intended metadata block (e.g. a Context References bullet reading '**Standards**: ...' inside the agent-authoring prose, not the artifact skeleton) -- so a naive file-wide grep for a field name inside an *agent definition* file (as opposed to the artifact it produces) can give a false-positive 'has this field' read.
